conceptual assets.information: The current grant identifies which requester owns the shared downstream bus and whether a request strobe is issued. Correct arbitration is required to prevent one requester from blocking or corrupting another requester’s transfer.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the state, select, and strobe logic determines the granted requester and the downstream request at lines 55, 79, 114, 118, 124, 128, and 158, so a fault could grant the wrong requester; availability is at risk because the same logic can withhold or continuously redirect the downstream request at lines 83, 113-130, and 158.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the arbiter state or selection so one requester is incorrectly granted or permanently denied service.

conceptual assets.information: The lock indication records whether the selected requester must retain the shared bus across multiple transfers. The bus switch depends on it to keep a locked sequence active and to control the downstream lock field.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because input lock fields are stored in locked and control transaction completion at lines 57, 88-103, and 111; availability is at risk because an incorrect lock state can hold the arbiter busy or terminate a locked sequence early at lines 90-103.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the stored lock indication to release another requester’s transaction early or hold the shared bus indefinitely.

conceptual assets.information: The address and read/write direction identify the downstream bus access selected from requester A or B. Downstream operation depends on these fields reaching the shared bus unchanged and belonging to the granted requester.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the select-controlled forwarding at lines 140 and 147 chooses which requester’s address and direction reach x_req_o, so a faulty selection can issue the wrong access.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could cause the switch to forward one requester’s address or direction with the other requester’s transfer.

conceptual assets.information: Acknowledgement and error status indicate whether the selected downstream transfer completed and whether it faulted. Requesters depend on these response fields to retire or retry their transfers.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because x_rsp_i acknowledgement and error fields are selectively delivered to the requester outputs at lines 164-169; availability is at risk because an altered acknowledgement can prematurely complete or indefinitely withhold a transfer.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress, fabricate, or route a downstream acknowledgement or error so a requester completes incorrectly or waits forever.

conceptual assets.information: Privilege and debug attributes qualify the requester’s authority for the forwarded bus access. Downstream protection and debug behavior can depend on these attributes.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the switch forwards the selected privilege and debug attributes at lines 144-145, so a faulty path can associate the wrong authority with a transfer; undermined expected behavior is at risk because the same fields directly propagate privileged or debug behavior to the downstream bus at lines 144-145.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could inject or misroute a privileged or debug-qualified request so normal access restrictions are bypassed.

conceptual assets.information: The target-selection decision identifies which enabled address region receives the request, including the fallback X target. Correct selection is required to prevent accesses from reaching the wrong downstream device.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because port_sel is computed from address-region comparisons at lines 356-361 and gates each downstream strobe at line 378; availability is at risk because an incorrect selection can suppress every valid target or route a request to an unusable target at lines 378 and 375-379.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt the address decode so a request is sent to the wrong gateway port or is not sent to any usable port.

conceptual assets.information: The request address and read/write direction identify the access forwarded to the selected gateway target. The selected downstream device depends on receiving the original access identity and direction.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because request records are copied to the selected output ports at lines 377 and 366-369, while the address also drives region selection at lines 356-361, so a corrupted path can perform a different access.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could modify or misassociate the forwarded address or read/write direction so a downstream device performs the wrong operation.

conceptual assets.information: The stored lock state records whether the monitored request is part of a locked sequence. The monitor uses it to decide when the request may complete.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because req_i.lock is stored in keeper.lock at line 420 and controls completion at line 426; availability is at risk because a corrupted lock state can terminate a locked sequence or prevent the monitor from releasing it.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter keeper.lock so a locked transfer is released prematurely or held after its response.

conceptual assets.information: The busy state, timeout count, halt suppression, and generated error record monitor an outstanding request and recover when a response does not arrive. Gateway operation depends on this state to avoid indefinite stalls.

conceptual assets.concept: Atomic operation operands and update result
conceptual assets.information: The asset is the selected atomic function together with its write operand, memory-read operand, and computed update value. The RMW operation depends on preserving these values and producing the corresponding system write and core response.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because operand and result values are held in arbiter.rdata, arbiter.wdata, and alu_res and leave through core_rsp_o.data or sys_req_o.data at lines 785, 813, and 826; integrity is at risk because the command and operands select and compute the write-back value at lines 778-779 and 838-845, so corruption changes the atomic update.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe the stored RMW operands or alter the command or ALU result so the memory update contains an incorrect value.

conceptual assets.concept: Atomic operation completion and fault status
conceptual assets.information: System acknowledgement and error status determine whether the atomic read or write phase completed and what status is returned to the core. The operation depends on these fields to advance and report correctly.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because sys_rsp_i.ack and sys_rsp_i.err are used to advance the phase and drive core_rsp_o at lines 786-801 and 827-828; availability is at risk because a missing or false acknowledgement can hold the operation in a wait state or complete it prematurely.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could fabricate or suppress a system acknowledgement or error so the atomic operation writes incorrectly or never completes.

conceptual assets.information: Privilege and debug attributes qualify the atomic access forwarded to the system bus. System-side protection and debug behavior can depend on these attributes.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because privilege and debug fields are forwarded from core_req_i to sys_req_o at lines 818-819; undermined expected behavior is at risk because those fields directly propagate privileged or debug behavior to the atomic system access.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could inject a privileged or debug-qualified atomic request and bypass normal system-side access restrictions.

conceptual assets.information: The control state records the idle, reserved, and conditional-store-wait phases of the load-reserved/store-conditional sequence. Correct state is required to permit the conditional store only in the intended sequence.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because state is changed by request type, reservation detection, and system acknowledgement at lines 910-927, thereby controlling the conditional-store decision; availability is at risk because state gates sys_req_o.stb at lines 943-946 and can suppress or hold the conditional store.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the reservation state to accept an unreserved store or to suppress every conditional store.

conceptual assets.information: The conditional-store result reports whether the store-conditional request failed and is encoded into the core response acknowledgement and data. Software depends on this result to know whether its reservation was honored.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because sc_fail is computed from the operation, request, and reservation state at line 957 and changes core_rsp_o.ack and core_rsp_o.data at lines 963-964, so corruption can report success for a failed store or failure for a successful one.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the failure result so software accepts an unperformed conditional store or unnecessarily retries a valid one.

conceptual assets.information: System acknowledgement and error status report completion or failure of the reservation-related bus transfer. The controller depends on acknowledgement to leave its pending state and on error status to report the transfer result.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because sys_rsp_i.ack advances the controller at lines 920-921 and sys_rsp_i.err is returned at line 962; availability is at risk because withholding acknowledgement leaves the controller in its pending state and blocks the operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress or fabricate the system acknowledgement or error so the reservation operation hangs or reports the wrong completion status.

conceptual assets.information: Privilege and debug attributes qualify the reservation or conditional-store access forwarded to the system bus. System-side protection and debug behavior can depend on these attributes.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because privilege and debug fields are copied from core_req_i to sys_req_o at line 942; undermined expected behavior is at risk because those fields directly propagate privileged or debug behavior to the reservation system access.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could inject a privileged or debug-qualified reservation request and bypass normal system-side restrictions.

considered, not kept.concept: Forwarded request and response payload data
considered, not kept.reason: The switch only forwards bus data between ports and does not store or compute from it, so the forwarded payload is barred by the forwarded-transaction and relayed-data rules.

considered, not kept.concept: Pending request flags and round-robin history
considered, not kept.reason: a_req, b_req, and sel_q only retain or bias a bus access while it is being served and therefore are handshake copies or arbitration bookkeeping rather than independent information.

considered, not kept.concept: Gateway address-map generics and port enables
considered, not kept.reason: A_BASE, A_SIZE, B_BASE, B_SIZE, C_BASE, C_SIZE, A_EN, B_EN, C_EN, and X_EN are build-time values that no RTL element can change at run time.
The gateway copies request and response data between ports without storing or computing from it, so relayed data is not a separate asset.

considered, not kept.concept: I/O device address-map generics and enables
considered, not kept.reason: DEV_SIZE, DEV_nn_BASE, DEV_nn_EN, and the derived device-map constants are build-time values that cannot be changed or withheld at run time.

considered, not kept.concept: I/O request and response staging copies
considered, not kept.reason: The neorv32_bus_reg instance and main_req/main_rsp only buffer or forward whole bus records between ports, which is excluded by the forwarded-transaction and port-buffer rules.
The switch only copies request data to device ports and merges response data without storing or computing from it, so the data is relayed data.

Address, handshake, lock, fence, and other fields that are only forwarded without being stored or interpreted as an independent decision are part of the forwarded transaction rather than separate assets.
The RVS unit forwards system response data and request data without storing or computing an independent data result, apart from the conditional-store status bit.
Clock and reset paths only time or reset the listed state and are excluded as conceptual assets by the clock-and-reset rule.

reply keys: the 2026-10-13 format as written in 'raw'; 'reply' holds it in v5 keys
